sense: put a new one in place of

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with in locum and the genitive
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.72 (Lewis & Short): in eōrum locum cīvēs Rōmānōs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to put instead or in the place of another, to substitute (class.)”.

terms.gloss: replace (what was lost or broken); put back
evidence: Tac. Ann. 1.63 (Lewis & Short): ruptōs vetustāte pontēs
Verg. A. 5.752 (Lewis & Short): flammīs ambēsa repōnunt rōbora nāvigiīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to replace, restore”. For putting a thing back where it was, see put away.

phrases.latin: Hoc frāctum est; aliud in ejus locum substituam.
phrases.english: This one’s broken; I’ll replace it.

sources: Lewis & Short: substituo · Lewis & Short: repono
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 185, 387.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
